newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli jets raid Hizbollah targets in s. Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Israeli jets raid Hizbollah targets in s. Lebanon.

text.p: Israeli jets attacked Hizbollah guerrilla targets in south Lebanon on Saturday hours after an Israeli-backed militia patrol was ambushed, security sources said.

They said the planes fired four rockets into Louwaizeh hills in Iqlim al-Toufah, a rugged ridge used by pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas to attack Israeli troops and their militia allies occupying a south Lebanon border zone.

The was no report of casualties in the air attack, which came hours after guerrillas ambushed a patrol of the Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia in Markaba in the zone. No one was hurt in the ambush, the SLA sources said.

No group immediately claimed responsibility for the Markaba attack but in Beirut, Hizbollah said in a statement its fighters fired "with appropriate weapons" at Israeli soldiers at Kassaret al-Ourosh on the edge of the zone and facing Iqlim al-Toufah.
The reported Hizbollah attack came shortly before the air raid, the fifth on Lebanon in little over two weeks.
After the air attack, Israeli artillery gunners fired heavy shells into Iqlim al-Toufah hills, security sources said.

The Syrian-backed Amal Movement said earlier in a statement that its guerrillas fired mortar bombs, anti-tank rockets and machineguns at an Israeli post at Qasseer and an SLA post at Alman to the northeast of Markaba and just inside the zone.
There was no immediate independent confirmation of the report.
Hizbollah and other guerrillas wage attacks against Israeli and SLA forces in a bid to drive them out from south Lebanon.

Some 1,000 Israeli troops and the 3,000-strong SLA hold the zone stretching along the Lebanese side of border from Mount Hermon in the east to the Mediterranean westwards since 1985 to ward off cross-frontier guerrilla raids on northern Israel.
